## Phase 4 inventory (at `ec365eb80`; re-measure on `eee52b084`)

> Superseded by the plan where they differ (phase 4 design round 1): the fallback is per-feature (a feature whose own prerequisite fails is deferred), cue-cache seeding is not a sufficient fixture, and "cue-cache bounds"/"countdown" do not exist in the original.


Source: `android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/debrify/app/tv/AndroidTvTorrentPlayerActivity.kt` at
`ec365eb80` (19,017 lines; class 136–19017, companion 18976–19016). Read-only survey of the main
checkout (no worktree, no build). The rules are those of the plan's **Phase 3 → Collaborator pattern**
(from `refactor/tvplayer-p3` at `043dfd1b8`): `internal class TvXController(activity: AppCompatActivity, host: Host)`,
verbatim moved members with declared substitutions, computed explicitly-qualified Host forwarders,
slot-anchored controller properties, `::x.isInitialized` through activity-owned getters, braced host
templates, cross-feature reads through the owning controller, teardown order unchanged, **no delegators**.

Method. A brace/string/comment-aware indexer resolved every depth-1 member of the class (960 members)
and its line span; a word-boundary scan (string templates included, comments excluded) mapped every
reference to its enclosing member; every hit list below was then checked by hand. "Patch" = one
token-level edit in a retained activity declaration (`foo` → `ctl.foo`), i.e. one checker `patched`
occurrence. "Substitution" = one declared edit inside a moved body (`foo` → `host.foo`, `this` →
`activity`). Line counts are body lines plus attached KDoc/comments.

**Phase-3 state assumed** (gone into controllers by the time phase 4 starts): sleep timer
(`TvSleepTimerController`; `SleepTimerMode` top-level), skip segments, Up Next card, IPTV recording
actions. Consequences for phase 4:
- `fireSleepTimer` (8070) is in the sleep controller; its `sendProgress(completed = false)` call goes
  through the activity's phase-3 Host forwarder `override fun sendProgress(completed: Boolean)`. Moving
  `sendProgress` means **patching a phase-3 pinned `added` span** (needs the checker's reviewed
  earlier-phase whitelist; none was expected in phase 3).
- `presentSkipSegment` (7947, now skip controller) reads `syncOverlay`, `linePickerOverlay`,
  `subtitlePanel`, `unifiedMenu` through phase-3 Host forwarders. **Keeping those four overlay
  references in the activity** avoids touching phase-3 pinned spans and keeps `SubtitleSyncDismissTest`
  unchanged (it reflects `syncOverlay`/`linePickerOverlay` on both player activities).
- `umPlaybackModel` (14658) already carries phase-3 call-site patches (`sleepTimerController.x`), and
  phase-3 `TvSleepTimerCharacterizationTest.unifiedMenuRowsDispatch…` reflects `umPlaybackModel` on the
  activity.
- Status pill was deferred out of phase 3 (no two-output delegators).

### Cross-cutting facts for phase 4

- **Shared handlers stay activity-owned and are borrowed.**
  - `externalSubtitleHandler` (1202) carries: the side-subtitle ticker (C4), the auto-sync ladder
    (8 s) and verify (90 s / 120 s) ticks, the auto-sync pill's announce-dismiss (5 s) and card-hide
    runnables, and the status pill's 1.4 s hide runnable. `onStop` (18040) removes only the ticker;
    `onDestroy` clears it wholesale at **18292**, *after* `releaseLoudnessEnhancer` (18263), `AudioEffectSession.closeCurrent` (18267), player release (18269–18286) and
    `subtitleScope.cancel()` (18245). No controller may own or clear it; every moved post/remove becomes
    `host.externalSubtitleHandler`.
  - `progressHandler` (1272) carries `progressRunnable` (5 s ticker: progress + Up Next + IPTV
    recovery + twin trial), the startup/manual-switch timeouts and the PikPak gate reprepare; cleared
    piecemeal at 18171–18179 and wholesale at **18258**. The progress reporter (feature 5) does **not**
    take the ticker; `progressRunnable`/`restartProgressUpdates` stay with the activity (phase 7).
  - `subtitleScope` (1147, Main + SupervisorJob) is shared with the addon-subtitle fetch (5014) and
    cancelled at **18245**: borrowed.
- **Overloads.** Every substituted `this` in features 1–6 flows into a parameter typed `Context`
  (`SubtitleSettings.*`, `ProfilePreferenceProjection.getBoolean`, `AudioEffectSession.open`,
  `UnifiedMenuSections.appearanceRows`, `AutoSyncRingView`, `TextView`/`LinearLayout`, `Toast.makeText`,
  `androidx.appcompat.app.AlertDialog.Builder`) or `Activity` (`SubtitleLinePickerController`,
  `SubtitleSyncOverlayController` — named argument `activity = this`). None is overloaded on
  Context/Activity/FragmentActivity/LifecycleOwner; no Glide or lifecycle-owner calls. Step T still
  records the bytecode descriptors (phase-3 audit tool) for each site.
- **Anonymous-object `this` (never substituted):** 14353 (ladder `Runnable`), 14373/14374 (verify
  `Runnable`, incl. the `autoSyncVerifyTick === this` identity check), 15130 (ticker `Runnable`).
  `this@AndroidTvTorrentPlayerActivity` → `activity`: 14247, 14344, 14453 (coroutine/Runnable bodies),
  13970 (`unifiedMenuCallbacks.stylePreview`).
- **`::x.isInitialized` in candidate code:** `::playerView` 14871 (`subtitlePanelCallbacks.onHidden`),
  14903, 14917 (`showSyncOverlay` lambdas); `::subtitleOverlay` 15067, 15081 (`onExternalSubtitleLoaded`),
  15110 (`stopExternalSubtitleRendering`). → activity getters `playerViewReady`, `subtitleOverlayReady`
  (`added`, slot-anchored, forwarded by Host).
- **Host methods with default/named arguments** must repeat the defaults in the Host interface and keep
  parameter names: `showSyncToast(glyph, accent, title, hint: String? = null, autoHideMs: Long?,
  uppercase: Boolean = true)` (called with named `autoHideMs`), `recordPlaybackLifecycle(event,
  details: String = "")` (1-arg calls in `deliverProgress`), `sendProgress(completed)` (named
  `completed =` at every caller), `runSubtitleAutoSync(auto: Boolean = false)` (0-arg call from the menu).
- **Volatile/threading:** no candidate field is `@Volatile`; all candidate code runs on the main thread
  except `withContext(Dispatchers.Default)` (aligner) / `Dispatchers.IO` (cue fetch) blocks, whose
  results are published back on Main. `TvPlaybackRecoveryStore.stageAsync/acknowledgeAsync` hop
  threads internally with already-built strings.
- **Reflection/name mangling:** a moved member that a test reflects by simple name must be `private` or
  a public member of the `internal` class (never `internal fun`). Affects feature 5 (`sendProgress`,
  `recoveryCompletedItemKeys`) and feature 6 (`umPlaybackModel`).
- **Split field blocks.** Every candidate's fields are spread over 2–3 non-adjacent blocks (listed per
  feature). The phase-3 rule anchors the controller property at the first removed field; the later
  removed fields have side-effect-free initializers except `subtitleSeekHandler` (1111, a main-looper
  `Handler`, created a few initializers earlier than today — no observable effect, but declare it).

for `subtitle_auto_sync_enabled` (as `NativePlayerSettingsConsumptionTest` does).

**Hazards:** three Runnable `this` (never substituted, identity check 14373); mutual calls with feature 3
(C4 → `startAutoSyncLadder`/`scheduleAutoSyncVerify`/`showSyncToast`/result writes; auto-sync →
`applySubtitleSettings`/`activeExternalSubtitleUrl`) — a logical cycle that the Host interfaces break at
compile time; `showSyncToast` defaults must be declared in the Host interface; `Log.d` (15323) vs
`android.util.Log` (destination import list).

**Proposed shape:**
```kotlin
internal class TvSubtitleAutoSyncController(private val activity: AppCompatActivity, private val host: Host) {
    interface Host {
        val speechTap: SpeechFeatureTap?
        val player: ExoPlayer?
        val subtitleScope: CoroutineScope
        val externalSubtitleHandler: Handler
        val externalSubtitleActive: Boolean          // → subtitle controller (owner)
        val activeExternalSubtitleUrl: String?       // → subtitle controller (owner)
        fun applySubtitleSettings()                  // → subtitle controller
        fun dp(value: Int): Int
    }
}
```
**Substitutions ≈ 53** (43 host + 6 `this` + 3 `this@` + 1 `findViewById`). **Activity patches: 14
standalone, 0 if moved with feature 3 + menu rows.** Size ≈ 516 + ≈ 30 structural ≤ 800.
**Risk: low–medium** (UI + background aligner; all timers on a borrowed handler; characterization
needs the aligner shadow).

subtitle menu-row builders**, as two controllers:

- **≈ 1,087 moved lines for 28 activity patches in 14 declarations** (≈ 0.026 patches/line, better than
  phase 3's ≈ 0.067), **zero test retargets, zero edits to phase-3 pinned spans**, ≈ 156 declared
  substitutions (≈ 23 `this`/`this@` sites for the overload audit, 6 `::isInitialized` via 2 new activity
  getters, 1 braced template), two companion consts moved file-private.
- Lifecycle edits are in-place token patches only: `onStart` 18001 (2), `onStop` 18040 (1), `onDestroy`
  18291 (2). `externalSubtitleHandler` (18292), `subtitleScope` (18245) and
  `SubtitleSettings.clear…Provider(this)` (18296) are untouched.
- If the reviewer rejects menu rows inside the subtitle controller: same two controllers without them,
  **≈ 1,006 lines / 45 patches (17 decls)**.
- Step-0 cost is the main risk: a deterministic `SubtitleAligner` shadow, a `SpeechFeatureTap`/cue-cache
  fixture and the profile pref projection, plus full characterization of the side renderer and track list.
  Step-T additions: multi-block field ownership with one slot anchor (and a negative), cross-controller
  Host forwarders (`this@AndroidTvTorrentPlayerActivity.subtitleAutoSync.x`), Host-interface default
  parameters (`showSyncToast`, `runSubtitleAutoSync`), a negative for rewriting the shadowed local
  `subtitleTracks` in `showSubtitleTrackDialog`, and the overload audit for the new `this` sites.

**Alternative** if engine characterization proves unreliable (like the phase-3 skip fallback): auto-sync
(1) + progress (3) ≈ 800 lines, 27 patches + 1 phase-3 forwarder + 6 retargets; or subtitle (2) +
progress (3) ≈ 855 lines, 49 patches.

**Deferred, with reasons:**
- **Progress reporter** → first item of the next phase (or a 4b mini-batch): good ratio, but it needs a
  reviewed edit to the phase-3 sleep forwarder, 5 reflective + 1 Dart anchor retargets, a visibility
  substitution for reflection, and it reads display state that later moves. Keeping it out keeps phase 4
  free of retargets.
- **Status pill** → phase 6 (34 of 40 call sites are in episode fetch / startup gate / source switcher);
  per-site patching is legal but the worst ratio (40 patches / 55 lines) and would be re-edited in phase 6.
- **Audio/display/speed/night/effects** → phase 7 with `playbackListener`, `setupPlayer` and
  `decoderAnalyticsListener` (20 of its 39 patches live there; native `LoudnessEnhancer` lifetime;
  `loadPlayerDefaults` mixed ownership; `nightModeIndex` reflection).
- **Unified-menu model** → last, or dissolved section-by-section into owning controllers (subtitle rows
  already in phase 4); moving it now creates a 61-member Host that every later phase would edit.

### Follow-ups found while mapping (not fixed)

- `onStop` removes only the side-subtitle ticker from `externalSubtitleHandler`; the auto-sync ladder
  (8 s, exits when no external subtitle) and verify (120 s, skipped while paused) ticks and pill runnables
  keep being posted while the activity is stopped.
- `autoSyncPillResultShowing` is write-only.
- Auto-sync pill and status pill views are never removed and their fade animators are never cancelled.
- `loadPlayerDefaults` mixes display/night/effects defaults with display-mode matching and skip-segment
  preferences.
- `showSubtitleTrackDialog` (dead) declares a local `subtitleTracks` that shadows the field.

## Phase 4 step 0 — original characterization at `eee52b084`

Both feature prerequisites passed **before** the remaining characterization:
`TvPhase4PrerequisiteTest` has seven tests, including 20 blocked alignment
runs and 20 uncached cue loads, superseded subtitle/URL loads, failure
fallback and destruction during pending work. Test-only aligner, audio-tap
and cue-fetch shadows retain the original `withContext(Default/IO)` and Main
publication, Handler scheduling, token guards and SupervisorJob. A test-only
CoroutineExceptionHandler observes otherwise uncaught worker errors without
changing the original dispatcher or Job; this allows verify's Error escape
and manual OOM conversion to be checked with named assertions. Cleanup
releases and settles workers, cancels test-owned work and closes overlays.
No feature is deferred.

The complete original characterization contains 61 tests: prerequisites 7,
manual sync 12, scheduling/lifecycle 7, verify 8, pill 5, external rendering 6,
and selection/settings/menu/overlay routing 16. The existing phase-1 ring
and phase-3 repaint tests remain unchanged. The original main-thread handler
and coroutine bodies execute throughout. Ladder boundary tests pause only
Robolectric's automatic vsync clock so animation frames cannot advance the
clock past an 8-second polling boundary; pill animation tests run frames and
check alpha, translation and duration. Infinite-pulse requests use
ShadowValueAnimator.actualRepeatCount (as phase 1 does); Robolectric ends
infinite animations after one cycle. Verify Error assertions compare type
and message because coroutine stack recovery can copy the Throwable.

Every new test has an original-code mutation proof below. Every mutation
ran in the detached original `p4/original` with the added tests; only one
original subtree changed at a time and was restored after each run. All 61
mutations are killed by a named JUnit AssertionError/ComparisonFailure;
none uses a compile failure, process exit or incidental exception as proof.
Exact before/after strings, patches, Gradle logs, XML, assertion stacks and
runners are in `p4/mutations/`, `p4/mutations.json` and `p4/run_mutations.py`.

their spans (attached KDoc/comments included); a word-boundary scan (string templates included,
comments excluded, hits qualified on another receiver excluded, `this@Activity.` hits included) mapped
every reference to its enclosing member and classified read/write/mutate/call; every list below was
then checked by hand. "Patch" = one token edit in a retained activity declaration. "Substitution" =
one declared edit inside a moved body. "Re-point" = a later edit of a pinned Host forwarder when its
target moves. Line counts include attached comments; a section banner separated from its declaration by
a blank line is counted only where stated (e.g. 10888–10899).

- **Shared IPTV core stays in the activity** (owner) and is read/written through computed Host
  forwarders by every IPTV candidate; it never needs a later re-point:
  `isIptvMode` 780, `iptvChannels` 781 (7 writers in 7 decls, 106 reads), `currentIptvIndex` 782
  (7 writers, 67 reads), `iptvSeriesAudioKey` 793, `currentIptvHttpHeaders` 801 (`@Volatile`),
  `iptvHlsForcedUrls` 806, `currentIptvStreamUrl` 910, `iptvSources` 928, `iptvSourceId` 934.
  Reasons: 7 of them are read by the phase-3 recording Host (8385–8391); the phase-2
  `IptvLiveLoadErrorPolicy` supplier in `setupPlayer` reads `iptvChannels`/`currentIptvIndex` on loader
  threads; reflective anchors: `TvIptvLoadPolicyCharacterizationTest` 34, 51–52, 59–65, 69, 86;
  `TvPlayerOriginalAccess` 218–219; `TvRecordingCharacterizationTest` 27, 28, 40, 42, 61, 87, 100;
  `TvRecordingMessagesCharacterizationTest` 62, 63, 93, 116, 129, 131;
  `TvRecordingBoundaryMessagesCharacterizationTest` 42, 76; `TvScheduleCharacterizationTest` 56, 112;

  `isIptvMode` also `StremioTvStartupWatchdogTest` 70, `TvSkipUiCharacterizationTest` 37,
  `TvUpNextCharacterizationTest` 37.
- **Borrowed handlers (activity-owned, never cleared by a controller):** `iptvBrowseHandler` 940 —
  B1 1 s settle + 2 s watch-registration fallback, B5 60 s archive-metadata retry, B9 deferred trim
  post (8939); cleared wholesale `onDestroy` **17464**. `progressHandler` 1286 — B2 20 s stall
  watchdog, B6 hide (4.5 s) / tick (1 s) `postAtTime` tokens; cleared wholesale **17511**. Note: the
  B1/B2 slot (939) and B3 slot (786) precede the initializers of `iptvBrowseHandler` (940) and
  `progressHandler` (1286); legal only because forwarders are computed (no construction-time read) —
  the existing "no Host member read during construction" negative covers it; add a fixture case.
- **Flutter bridge:** every candidate calls `MainActivity.getAndroidTvPlayerChannel()` directly or a
  phase-2 top-level request (`requestIptvStreamUrls`, `reportIptvStreamResult`, `requestIptvEpg`); no
  seam is needed — step 0 uses the existing `TvPlayerRecordingMessenger` fake with main-looper replies.

  `Runnable { … return@Runnable }` (13083), `runOnUiThread { … return@runOnUiThread }` (12945, labels
  survive `activity.runOnUiThread {`); B3 `object : MethodChannel.Result` (9994–10085) with local

- **Braced templates — retained patches too:** `recordPlaybackLifecycle` 14899

  patches must be `${progressReporter.progressSentCount}` / `${progressReporter.progressAckCount}` (an

  keep their JVM backing-field name under any Kotlin visibility (A `recoveryCompletedItemKeys`).
- **Volatile/threading:** no candidate field is `@Volatile`; all candidate code runs on main
  (MethodChannel results, `runOnUiThread`, main-looper handlers). `TvPlaybackRecoveryStore.stageAsync/
  acknowledgeAsync` hop internally with already-built strings (unchanged).
- **No `::x.isInitialized` in any phase-5 candidate** (no new activity readiness getters).

`isStremioTvMode && startupSourcesExhausted`, the startup cursor, the manual-switch snapshot and

### B. IPTV live — can it be split?

**Answer: partly.** The plan's "one unit: shared token protocol" holds for the **guide + browse + zap
paging + channel switch (+ `initIptvMode`)** core only. Five satellites own their state cleanly (all
writers inside the unit) or own nothing but a token, and can move before the core:

| unit | owns its state cleanly? | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| B1 watch registration + startup-channel memory | **yes** | `iptvWatchRegistrationToken`, `lastLiveChannel*`: every writer/reader inside |
| B2 Stremio resolve + candidate ladder (incl. `beginIptvPlayback`) | **yes** | all 6 ladder fields written only inside; `iptvStremioToken` 1 writer (`beginIptvPlayback`); outside reads only (5 refs) |
| B2′ ladder *without* `beginIptvPlayback` | no | 14 of its 23 inbound refs are `beginIptvPlayback` resetting/initialising ladder state (12916–12961) |
| B3 Start Over / catch-up | **token only** | `iptvCatchupToken` has 2 outside bumps (419, 10827); the 3 flags `iptvStartOverActive/Loading/TimelineVisible` have 9 outside writes in 3 decls (`performIptvLiveRetune`, `playbackListener`, `switchToIptvChannel`) and 3 outside reads → stay host (sleep-latch precedent) |
| B6 zap banner | **yes** | 29 fields, all writers inside; outside reads `iptvZapBanner` ×3, `iptvZapBannerDocked` ×3 |
| B5 EPG now/next + guide header | owns nothing | entry EPG state lives on `IptvChannelEntry`; header views bound by `initIptvMode` |
| B4 EPG schedule pane | yes, but costly | pane fields clean except `iptvEpgAdapter` (created by `setupIptvOverlay` 8614) and `iptvEpgEntry` (read by guide callbacks 8617/8620, keys 6804); 9 view binds in `initIptvMode` → 33 patches |
| B7 live dock styling | yes (2 maps) | but writes host `cinemaSeekMode`/`cinemaSeekWasPlaying`; Host = 30 control-dock views |
| B8 VOD/episode nav | no | `iptvSeriesAudioKey` written by `initIptvMode`, `requestIptvCatchup`, `switchToIptvChannel` |
| B9 core | **must move as one** | protocol table below |

**Token/generation fields** (writers / readers by declaration; full matrix in Appendix 2):

| field | writers | readers | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `iptvUiContextToken` 954 | beginIptvAllCategorySearch, restoreIptvCategoryAfterSearch, requestIptvBrowse, beginIptvCategoryZapSession, activateIptvZapUiContext, onDestroy 17466 | requestIptvBrowse ×3, requestIptvZapPage ×4 | **core (shared guide↔zap)** |
| `iptvBrowseToken` 938 | same 5 + onDestroy 17467 | requestIptvBrowse ×3 | core |
| `iptvZapRequestToken` 949 | beginIptvAllCategorySearch, restoreIptvCategoryAfterSearch, requestIptvBrowse, beginIptvCategoryZapSession, requestIptvChannelJump, requestIptvZapPage, disableIptvZapPaging, activateIptvZapUiContext, onDestroy 17468 | requestIptvChannelJump ×3, requestIptvZapPage ×6 | core |
| `iptvZapOwnsUiContext` 955 | initIptvMode, beginIptvAllCategorySearch, restoreIptvCategoryAfterSearch, requestIptvBrowse, beginIptvCategoryZapSession, requestIptvChannelJump, activateIptvZapUiContext | beginIptvAllCategorySearch, requestIptvBrowse ×3, bootstrapInitialIptvZapPaging, requestIptvZapPage ×3, activateIptvZapUiContext | core |
| `iptvZapRequestInFlight` 950 | 15 writes in 8 decls (guide search ×2, browse, 4 zap fns, onDestroy 17469) | setupIptvOverlay, requestIptvZapPage, prefetchIptvZapPage, drainPendingIptvZapInputs, prefetchAdjacentIptvCategory, requestAdjacentIptvCategory | core |

second phase would re-point ≈ 25 pinned forwarders.

and view-tree characterization across classic + GLASS/EDITION/CONSOLE from zero.

### Ordering for the rest of IPTV

1. **Phase 5:** A + B1/B2 + B3 (above).
2. **IPTV-2:** B6 zap banner (two classes; Host reads zap state, `formatEpgTime`/`ensureIptvChannelEpg`
   from the activity, re-pointed in step 3).
3. **IPTV-3 (one unit, multi-file):** B9 core + B4/B5 EPG + B8 VOD/episodes, one owner per token; re-points
   ≈ 25 forwarders created in steps 1–2.
4. **With the controls/dock-skin phase:** B7 live dock styling.
5. **With the playback core:** tune pipeline, twin trial, live recovery, reconnect pill (and the
   `progressHandler`/`progressRunnable` ticker).

## Phase 5 step 0 — characterization of `1a33c42cb`

Production is unchanged. Added **44 tests** against the original activity: 18 progress,
13 channel-start/ladder, 12 Start Over and one recording handoff. The shared
`TvPhase5OriginalTest` reuses the typed original reflection selectors and recording binary
messenger. Tests use paused loopers and a dynamic ExoPlayer, real lifecycle stop/destroy
where needed, and the existing fake MediaStore provider for the outgoing tee. No production
seam or helper retarget has been added.

Progress covers periodic/paused/completed/sleep/final maps for single, series, collection
and IPTV VOD; payload updates and visible playlist refresh before bridge delivery;
held-resume/raw-position completion, inclusive thresholds, cumulative completion sets and
parse resets; startup/manual/missing-item guards; maintenance/activity maps; logging boundaries
and bridge availability. Existing watchdog reflection contracts remain covered by the
unchanged baseline suite.

The recovery prerequisite reflects the store's separate **writer ExecutorService**. A latch
blocks an entered writer task without holding the recovery-store monitor; all waits are
bounded to five seconds and cleanup releases/drains it. Ordinary checkpoints remain queued,
while final/completed/local-completion checkpoints persist before bridge delivery or
pause/release. Snapshot identities/defaults/flags and eligibility guards are pinned.
Delayed out-of-order true ACKs remove only their own session/sequence; false, error, missing
and thrown delivery do not ACK. A delayed ACK after actual activity destruction still works.
A player-read failure outside the delivery catch preserves the original difference:
`onStop` leaves `finalProgressSnapshot` true, while `finish` and `onDestroy` clear it in
`finally`. This is recorded in Follow-ups and is not fixed.

Channel tests pin the complete watch/settle maps, two-second watch fallback and one-second
memory deadline, repeat-channel token supersession, eligibility reads at callback time and
preferred twins. The ladder pins finalize/reset/URL-clear/stop/resolve ordering, candidate
and source-row order, token and finishing guards, advancement/exhaustion strings, twenty-second
stall boundary, winner deduplication and manual rearming. The real outgoing tee publishes
its exact bytes before token reset, URL clear, stop and an empty resolution response.
Start Over pins call-time default dispatch, all button labels/content descriptions/visibility,
catch-up maps and guards, guide-versus-controls relevance, same-entry token supersession,
retained flags, replay metadata/defaults, timeline/focus timing and Go Live ordering.
Explicit cancellation, stop, destroy and the player-error return-to-live path reject late
archive replies without clearing newer loading.

### Original-code mutation table

Every new test has one named assertion-killed mutation on detached **`1a33c42cb` + the five
new test files**, under `p5/original/`. Each run cleans JVM test results and selects exactly
one named test. **44/44 killed**; compilation failures, incidental crashes and zero-test runs
are not accepted. Full exact before/after strings, enclosing PSI selectors, patches, Gradle
logs, XML and assertion stacks are in `p5/mutations/` and `p5/mutation-table.json`.
The temporary original worktree has been removed.

| Proof | Named test (class::method) | Original mutation | Failing assertion |
|---|---|---|---|
| g01 | `TvProgressReporterCharacterizationTest::periodicPausedAndCompletedPayloadsPreserveEveryArgumentAndStableDuration` | `"sourceIndex" to currentStremioSourceIndex` → `"sourceIndex" to (currentStremioSourceIndex + 1)` | Exact paused periodic map: sourceIndex expected 3, got 4. |
| g02 | `TvProgressReporterCharacterizationTest::localCompletionUsesRawPositionInclusiveThresholdAndCumulativeDeduplication` | `>= completionThreshold` → `> completionThreshold` | At the inclusive 80% boundary localCompleted expected true, got false. |
| g03 | `TvProgressReporterCharacterizationTest::heldResumeTargetNeverFabricatesLocalCompletionAndCompletionUsesDuration` | `else heldResumePositionMs(rawPosition) ?: rawPosition` → `else rawPosition` | Held resume target: positionMs expected 95000, got 25000. |

## Phase 5 step 0b — controlled programme-time boundaries

Six new original-surface cases pin start/stop at now − 1 ms, exactly now and now + 1 ms.
Robolectric instrumentation of the original activity and future controller routes their
System.currentTimeMillis calls through the paused clock; the test explicitly sets/verifies
that clock. No real-time waits or production seam. At exact start the request is accepted;
at exact stop it is past replay. An airing request stays airing when its reply arrives after
the stop time, pinning request-time capture.

The complete moved-code sweep finds two programme comparisons in requestIptvCatchup
(startMs > now and now < stopMs), both covered on either side and at equality. The other
moved time comparison is progress logging's inclusive 60-second elapsed boundary, already
pinned and assertion-killed by step-0 g13; recovery updatedAtMs reads have no time comparison.
No channel-start method has a now/startMs/stopMs comparison. Earlier IptvEntryRules stays frozen.

| Proof | Named test | Original mutation | Failing assertion |
|---|---|---|---|
| b01 | `TvIptvCatchupClockBoundaryTest::futureStartOneMillisecondAheadDoesNotRequestOrMutateLoadingAndToken` | `programme.startMs > now` → `programme.startMs > now + 1` | java.lang.AssertionError: future programme is rejected expected:<0> but was:<1> |
| b02 | `TvIptvCatchupClockBoundaryTest::exactStartIsRequestedAsAiringWithLoadingAndOriginalStartPayload` | `programme.startMs > now` → `programme.startMs >= now` | java.lang.AssertionError: programme starting exactly now is requested expected:<1> but was:<0> |
| b03 | `TvIptvCatchupClockBoundaryTest::startOneMillisecondAgoIsStillRequestedAsAiring` | `programme.startMs > now` → `programme.startMs >= now - 1` | java.lang.AssertionError: past start remains eligible expected:<1> but was:<0> |
| b04 | `TvIptvCatchupClockBoundaryTest::exactStopIsPastReplayWithoutStartOverLoadingOrLiveFlags` | `now < programme.stopMs` → `now <= programme.stopMs` | java.lang.AssertionError: stop boundary selects start-over versus replay expected:<false> but was:<true> |
| b05 | `TvIptvCatchupClockBoundaryTest::stopOneMillisecondAheadIsAiringEvenWhenReplyArrivesAfterStop` | `now < programme.stopMs` → `now + 1 < programme.stopMs` | java.lang.AssertionError: stop boundary selects start-over versus replay expected:<true> but was:<false> |
| b06 | `TvIptvCatchupClockBoundaryTest::stopOneMillisecondAgoIsPastReplay` | `now < programme.stopMs` → `now - 2 < programme.stopMs` | java.lang.AssertionError: stop boundary selects start-over versus replay expected:<false> but was:<true> |

`1a33c42cb` (phase-4 merge, 17,205 lines; class header 136, companion 17171–17205). This is a read-only
survey of the main checkout: no worktree, no build, nothing under `../debrify-wt/`. The rules are the
plan's **Phase 3 → Collaborator pattern**, plus the phase-3 post-review tightening and the phase-4 step-T
additions:

- `internal class TvXController(private val activity: AppCompatActivity, private val host: Host)`.
- A compiled overload audit of every substituted `this`, covering constructors, context aliases and the
  reviewed list of anonymous `Runnable`/`object` receivers.

Method: the phase-5 indexer (`scratchpad/p5/idx.py`, brace/string/comment-aware, now in `scratchpad/p6/`)
resolved all **869** depth-1 class members and their spans, including attached KDoc. A word-boundary scan
then mapped every reference to its enclosing member and classified it as read, write, mutate or call. That
scan includes string templates and `this@Activity.` hits. It excludes comments and hits qualified on
another receiver.

- An aggregator (`p6/agg.py`) splits the inbound references of any candidate set into four groups:
  - retained-activity patches;
  - references from members that phase 5 moves (these become phase-5 Host forwarders, so they count as
    **re-points**);
  - references from pinned phase-3/4 Host spans;
  - references between controllers inside the set.
- A receiver audit (`p6/recv.py`) lists every host/`this`/inherited reference inside a lambda with
  receiver or an anonymous object.

Every list below was then checked by hand. "Patch" means one token edit in a retained activity
declaration. "Substitution" means one declared edit inside a moved body.

**Phase-5 state assumed** (A progress reporter, B1/B2 IPTV channel start + Stremio ladder, B3 Start Over;
being executed elsewhere and treated as controllers). Their 42 member declarations at this SHA are listed
in `p6/p5decls.txt`. References from them into phase-6 candidates are counted as **phase-5 forwarder
re-points**, not patches:

- progress reporter → gate state: `startupFailoverCursor`, `startupSourcesExhausted`,
  `manualSourceSwitchSnapshot`, `manualSourceRestoreInProgress`;
- channel-start ladder → switcher: `setupStremioSources`, `updateStremioQualityBadge`,
  `watchSourceSwitchOutcome`, `dropStaleSourceSwitchFeedback`.

In the other direction, phase-6 code reads the phase-5 ladder in three places, always via the owning
controller: `iptvStremioChannelKey` ×2 (14988, 15834) and `switchToIptvStremioSource` ×1 (15835). The
banner and the Stremio TV guide have **zero** references to or from phase-5 members.

**Phase-3/4 pinned spans touched:** only the subtitle controller's Host. It forwards `hideStatusPill`
(1148), `showStatusPill` (1161) and `showStatusPillTransient` (1162); these become 3 re-points when the
status pill moves. No other pinned forwarder names a phase-6 candidate. `isStremioTvMode` is forwarded by
the Up Next Host at 170 but stays in the activity.

### Cross-cutting facts for phase 6

- **Shared state that stays in the activity** (its owner) and is reached by computed Host forwarders,
  never mirrored:
  - `stremioSources` 1019 (`var`, mutated in place). Readers and writers span the playback core, the
    phase-5 ladder, the Stremio TV media start, the unified menu, `parsePayload`, the gate and the
    switcher.
  - `currentStremioSourceIndex` 1020. It has 8 writers across gate, switcher, fetch, the Stremio TV media
    start, the phase-5 ladder and `parsePayload`.
  - `stremioResolutionToken` 1023. Writers: gate ×2, switcher ×1, episode fetch ×2. Readers:
    `resolveAndPlay` ×3, `discoverProtectedMime` ×2, switcher ×10, episode fetch ×4. This is a token
    shared with playback start, so it gets one owner later, with playback start.
  - `hasPlaylistResolver` 1024: navigation ×7, `parsePayload` writes it.
  - `isStremioTvMode` 1107: 12 readers, the Up Next Host forwarder, and three reflective tests.
  - The "load more" payload configuration (1088–1095, 1102–1104): `seriesSourceTabs`,
    `seriesPacksFetched`, `seriesEpisodesFetched`, `movieMoreSources`, `movieSourcesFetched`,
    `moreSourcesLoadingMode`, `sourceAddons`, `addonFetchState`, `addonPackProbing`. `parsePayload`,
    `bindViews` (source-browser callbacks) and `umSourcesModel` write or read it. Making it
    controller-owned would add **+30 patches** (S2 alone goes from 7 to 37 inbound).
  - Nested `data class TvSourceAddon` 1101 is public and referenced only at 1102 and 16125. It **stays**
    with `sourceAddons`; moving it would change its binary name.
  - The lateinit views `startupGateView` 140 and `startupGateStatus` 141 are set reflectively by
    `StremioTvStartupWatchdogTest:51–52,253`. `pikPakReactivationIndicator`/`Text` 1304/1305 are set by
    the watchdog test (:55) and by `TvPhase3OriginalTest:44`. The `nextOverlay`/`nextText`/`nextSubtext`/
    `nextBackdrop` views at 156–161 are set by the watchdog test (:54) and by `TvPhase3OriginalTest:43`.
- **Borrowed handlers** (the activity owns them; a controller never clears them):
  - `progressHandler` 1293 is used by the banner hide/tick `postAtTime` tokens, the gate's five watchdog
    `Runnable`s, the 10 s switcher and guide waits, the 30 s recovery-fetch fallback and the 1.5 s Stremio
    TV hide. It is cleared wholesale at `onDestroy` **16453**.

### C. Source switcher + startup/manual-switch gate + "fetch more sources" recovery, with PikPak retry and status pill (one cluster)

The plan's "move together" holds, and the measurement explains why:

- **The gate's own state is playback-core state.** 75 of the cluster's 114 activity references sit in
  `playbackListener` (27), `resolveAndPlay` (16), `onDestroy` (18), `parsePayload` (7) and
  `iptvDiagAnalyticsListener` (5), plus `bindViews`/`onCreate`/`sendFinished`.
- **Gate ↔ switcher coupling is two-way and dense:** 51 switcher→gate references against 7 gate→switcher.

**Unit split** (all lines at `1a33c42cb`):

**Timers / handlers / teardown:**

- **G:** five `Runnable`s on the borrowed `progressHandler`:
  - startup timeout (12 s, re-arms itself every 3 s via `postDelayed(this, …)` while
    `startupWatchdogShouldExtend` allows, capped at 45 s, or 120 s for PikPak);
  - startup commit check (200 ms metadata grace);
  - manual-switch timeout (12 s + 3 s re-arm);
  - manual commit check (200 ms);
  - `pikPakGateReprepare` (4 s; the captured `pikPakRetryId` and `mediaPreparationGeneration` are compared
    at fire time).
  - Also a 30 s recovery-fetch fallback (14766) and a `post { failStartupCandidate("missing-source") }`
    (14819).
  - All five fields are cleared explicitly at `onDestroy` 16366–16375, then
    `startupFailoverGeneration++` and the cursor is nulled (16379–16380). These **15 statements stay in
    place as patches** before `startupGateView` is hidden at 16381 (the view stays in the activity).
- **S1a:** a 10 s switch-outcome timeout on `progressHandler`, plus a `Player.Listener` on the player;
  `cancelSourceSwitchWait` at `onDestroy` **16502** becomes a patch in place.
- **S2:** no timers, only `runOnUiThread` callbacks guarded by `isFinishing`/`isDestroyed`.
- **PK:** owns `pikPakRetryHandler` (1.5 s exhausted → `playNext` at 6499) and an untracked local
  `checkHandler` that polls every 500 ms (existing follow-up). Cancelled at:
  - `onPause` **16321**, the only feature cancelled in `onPause`;
  - `onDestroy` **16415/16416**;
  - 7 navigation sites.
- **PILL:** 1.4 s hide on the borrowed `externalSubtitleHandler`, retired at 16487.
- **EF:** none.

Each cross-unit edge is a computed Host forwarder through the owning controller, which comes to ≈ 45
cross forwarders. The Host objects in the activity total **≈ 150–160 forwarders (≈ 200 lines)**. Add
2 readiness getters: `startupGateStatusReady`, `pikPakReactivationIndicatorReady`.

**Initializer timing:**

- G at slot 1030 runs 1059 and 1063–1072 earlier than their original positions (11 constants:
  `false`/`null`/`0L`) — they move past activity fields 1049–1058, including
  `recoveryStartedAtMs = System.currentTimeMillis()`, which stays put.

  proofs are needed.

**Substitutions (≈ 590):** G ≈ 192 (128 host incl. 4 braced, 17 cross, 9 Android, **≈ 38 visibility**:
nearly every gate member is touched from outside, the measure of how little the gate is encapsulated),
S1a ≈ 103 (incl. 9 braced), S1b ≈ 85, BADGE ≈ 20, S2 ≈ 83, PK ≈ 44, PILL ≈ 16, EF ≈ 49.

**Hazards:**

- **`pikPakRetryId`** is a shared token. G captures it at schedule time and compares it at fire time
  inside the `Runnable` (14859, 14865, 14867); S1b writes it with `++`; PK owns it. It needs one owner
  (PK) and computed forwarders, so it is read at fire time and never snapshotted.
- **`stremioResolutionToken`** is shared with playback start (Host `var`).
- **`startupFailoverGeneration`** is read 4× by the retained `resolveAndPlay` inside async callbacks, so
  the read stays live through `startupGate.x`.
- **`finish()`** in G (14790) must dispatch to the override.
- **Two-way G↔S1 forwarders:** G is constructed first (slot 1030) and must reach S1 only through computed
  forwarders, with no construction-time read. The plan already covers this with a negative.
- 13 braced templates.
- Runnable self `this` ×6.
- `onDestroy` keeps 18 in-place patches with **order unchanged**.
- The exhaustive checker must treat the 3 field-less controllers' slots as anchored `added` declarations.

**Risk: high.** This is the most stateful, async and teardown-heavy unit left outside the playback core.
Existing characterization is narrow (the watchdog test, 13 cases) and the Dart contracts are text-only.

**Step-0 gaps:**

- Startup gate: eligibility matrix (IPTV, Stremio TV, aiostreams, PikPak, single vs multi attempt),
  12 s timeout, 3 s re-arm with the 45 s/120 s caps, 200 ms commit grace, error-slate and duration
  checks, failover to the next source, recovery fetch with its 30 s fallback, exhaustion → toast + finish
  + `startupSourcesExhausted`, the `startupSourceFailed` payload.
- Manual switch: snapshot/restore transaction (`manualSourceRestoreInProgress`, `perItemImdbIds` restore,
  `playItem(..., suppressTrakt = true)`), stale-token resolve rejection, switch-outcome listener and 10 s
  timeout with pill messages, `dropStaleSourceSwitchFeedback`.
- `switchToSourcePlaylist`: episode-targeting matrix (exact episode, missing-episode toast), shuffle
  reset, metadata re-request.
- `switchToStremioSource`: PikPak branch re-arming `pikPakRetryId`, the IPTV branch handing off to the
  phase-5 ladder.
- Fetch more and addon fetch: fetched flags, probing set, adopt with the preferred-source-missing toast,
  failure paths.
- PikPak: metadata wait (5 s, buffering not an error), backoff 2/4/8/16/18 s, exhaustion → shuffle/manual/
  startup failure or `playNext` after 1.5 s, the overlay, `onPause` cancellation.
- Pill: ensure/show/transient 1.4 s/hide, and the shared-handler interplay with the subtitle ticker.
- The JVM baseline must include the existing watchdog cases before the helper retarget.

### D. "Next" overlay (auto-advance / loading overlay): do not move standalone

**Owned:** `nextOverlay` 156, `nextText` 157, `nextSubtext` 158 and `nextBackdrop` 161 (lateinit views,
bound at `bindViews` 2444–2447). Functions: `showNextOverlay@8094`, `fadeInNextOverlay@8100`,
`hideNextOverlay@8107`, `setNextOverlayBackdrop@5796`. That is 41 lines. The image branch is dead: the
only caller, 5791, passes `null`.

**Inbound: 25 references in 6 declarations:**

- `bindViews` ×4 (writes);
- `playbackListener` 1671, 1673, 1683, 1685;
- `setResolvingState` 5786–5791 (5);
- `isCleanPlaybackState` 8128; `showBufferingIndicatorDebounced` 16328;
- Stremio TV `requestStremioTvNext` ×10.

**Hazards:** `::nextBackdrop.isInitialized` (5797) needs a readiness getter; 2 `Glide.with(this)` calls;
2 reflective field sets (`StremioTvStartupWatchdogTest:54`, `TvPhase3OriginalTest:43`).

**Verdict:** the patch/line ratio is about 0.6. The overlay belongs to the loading overlay
(`setResolvingState`, called from `resolveAndPlay` and the gate), so move it with title/OTT identity and
the loading overlay in the controls/presentation phase. Until then the Stremio TV and gate controllers
forward `nextText`, `nextSubtext`, `fadeInNextOverlay()`, `hideNextOverlay()` and `setResolvingState()`.

**The IPTV zap banner, classic + styled, as option (ii)**:
`TvIptvZapBannerController` (≈ 660) + `TvIptvZapBannerStyledRenderer` (≈ 700).

  any unit in the file. There are 0 test retargets, 0 Dart anchors, 0 lifecycle edits and no async
  protocol. It is independent of phase 5 (0 references either way).
- It completes p5's queued "IPTV-2", and it shrinks the IPTV core that a later phase must move by 1,304
  lines.
- Cost: ≈ 281 substitutions (122 `dp`, 42 overload-audit sites incl. 4 Glide), 8 inert-initializer proofs,
  1 Host of 19 read-only forwarders, and characterization from zero across 4 styles.
- **Step-T additions:**
  - a controller constructing a sibling renderer in its initializer (pinned structural span; negative:
    the renderer reads A or the host during construction);
  - an explicit cross-object qualifier (`classic.`) substitution class with an occurrence count;
  - a negative for an unqualified A-name left in B, proven by a compile failure in the fixture;
  - a Host read inside a moved default-argument expression;
  - 42 compiled overload descriptors.

**Alternative** if characterization budget is the constraint: STV-lite (529 lines, 16 patches,
1 retarget). It is below the 800 floor. No cohesive partner exists to pad it: the Next overlay and the
media trio both worsen the ratio. It fits as a short phase 7.

### Honest estimate of the activity's final size

What **necessarily remains** under the current rules (verbatim moves, no delegators, unchanged class
header, activity owns lifecycle and teardown order):

| item | lines (est.) |
|---|---|
| imports (shrinks as code leaves) | ≈ 100 |
| class header, companion (`PAYLOAD_KEY` + residual constants) | ≈ 30 |
| shared state and single-owner fields: player/trackSelector/payload/`currentIndex`/`playlistMode`, Stremio source list + index + resolution token, IPTV core list/index/sources/headers (`@Volatile`)/forced URLs, `isIptvMode`/`isStremioTvMode`, handlers and scopes, ≈ 32 lateinit views, recovery/session ids, presets | ≈ 450–650 |
| controller properties with Host objects: today 6 controllers = 141 lines; ≈ 28–32 controllers at about 25–35 lines each, with the gate, IPTV core and playback start being wide | ≈ 750–1,000 |
| readiness getters (`::x.isInitialized`) | ≈ 15–25 |
| lifecycle: `onCreate` 173, `onStart`/`onStop`/`onResume`/`onPause` ≈ 100, `onDestroy` 169 (43-step order; becomes controller-qualified but stays), `finish` 17, `onRequestPermissionsResult` 11, `setupBackPressHandler` 43, buffering indicator 21, `recordPlaybackLifecycle` 9 | ≈ 545 |
| `bindViews` (lateinit view binding the activity owns; per-feature parts can leave) and `parsePayload` (writes about 30 owner fields; a struct return would be non-verbatim) | ≈ 200–360 |
| **Subtotal, with routers extracted** | **≈ 2,100–2,700** |
| `playbackListener` + `dispatchKeyEvent` if they stay verbatim | +875 |
| **Realistic end state** | **≈ 2,800–3,600** |

**The activity can never reach ≤ 800 lines under these rules.** The Host wiring alone is about 800 lines,
and it grows as code leaves: each 1,000 lines extracted adds roughly 40–100 lines of forwarders. The end
state needs the documented exception the plan already anticipates. The remaining responsibilities are:

- Android entry point and manifest FQN;
- lifecycle order;
- composition root (controller properties, Host objects);
- the shared player and single-owner state;
- payload intake;
- possibly the two routers.

Its exit milestone would be a separate, reviewed rule change, for example moving Host objects into the
activity's class header (the activity implements the Host interfaces), or allowing non-verbatim router
splits. That is not part of this series.

#### Follow-ups pinned as-is (no fixes)

- Guide-data replies have no switch-token guard; valid late data still applies.
  Partial replies leave omitted/malformed entries loading; a null bridge leaves
  requested rows loading and a channel switch in progress with its new marks.
- `cancelGuideWait` removes from the **current** player. Swapping players before
  cancellation leaves the old player's listener registered; capture/ownership
  changes belong in separate behavioral work.
- `onDestroy` does not bump the switch token or explicitly cancel guide wait.
  Both wait field references remain; the existing wholesale progress-handler
  cleanup removes the pending timeout. No teardown step was added or reordered.

Source: `android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/debrify/app/tv/AndroidTvTorrentPlayerActivity.kt` at `a4ed4f368`
(phase-6 merge, **15,167 lines**, class header 136, companion 15133–15166). Read-only survey of the main
checkout: no worktree, no build, nothing under `../debrify-wt/`. Phase 7 (Stremio TV guide "lite", branch
`refactor/tvplayer-p7`, design + step T/0 committed, not merged) is treated as a controller: its 30
members, 16 activity patches and 12-member Host are taken from its plan section. All phase 3–6 collaborator
rules apply (AppCompatActivity injection + compiled overload audit incl. constructors/aliases/Runnable
receivers; computed, explicitly-qualified Host forwarders; slot-anchored controller properties; an inert
proof for **every** moved property that runs after the controller's first slot, no contiguous exemption;
activity-owned `isInitialized` getters; braced host templates; cross-feature reads via the owning
controller; no delegators; teardown order unchanged; ≤ 800 lines per file; nested destination construction
allowed with effective-slot mapping).

Method: the phase-6 indexer (`scratchpad/p6/idx.py`) re-run on `a4ed4f368` (**788** depth-1 members), a
word-boundary reference scan per name (string templates and `this@Activity.` hits included; comments and
foreign-receiver hits excluded), an owner map over the four units plus the ten existing controller
properties, and a receiver audit of every reference inside `object :`/`Runnable {`/scope lambdas. Every
list below was then checked by hand against the source. Working files: `scratchpad/p8/` (`units8.py`,
`inbound.py`, `recv8.py`, `inb_*.txt`, `out_gate1.txt`, `hostneeds.txt`, `shared.txt`). Counts reproduce the
phase-6 inventory's figures for the same units (46/10/2/3 members; 630/308/417/43 lines), so the units were
not changed by phases 5–6, only shifted.

"Patch" = one token edit in a retained activity declaration. "Re-point" = one edited Host forwarder in an
existing controller property (a `patched` row on that whole activity property, as phase 5 did for the sleep
forwarder). "Substitution" = one declared edit inside a moved body.

---

### Summary and recommendation

| option | lines out | activity edits | edits/line | Host | proofs | Kotlin test retargets | Dart edits | lifecycle patches |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **W** whole gate-1 (G+S1a+S1b+BADGE) | 1,398 (+9 companion) | **109** patches in 25 decls + **8** re-points (2 properties) + 1 visibility patch | 0.084 | 1 × 53 (nested) | **31** | 45 watchdog sites (helper) + 7 progress-test sets + 1 field (8 map entries + `call` routing) | **8** | 16 (`onDestroy` 14328–14342, 14464) |
| **S** switcher first (S1a+S1b+BADGE) | **768** | **23** patches in 19 decls + **4** re-points (1 property) + 1 visibility patch | **0.036** | 1 × 51 | **1** | 1 map entry (`sourceSwitchReadyListener`) | **3** | 1 (`onDestroy` 14464) |
| then G (phase 9) | 630 (+9) | 93 patches + 4 p5 re-points + 11 S-Host re-points | 0.172 | 1 × ≈ 32 | 29 | as W minus the field entry | 5 | 15 |
| BADGE alone | 43 | 6 patches in 4 decls | 0.14 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| S1a+BADGE alone (no applier) | 351 | 25 patches + 4 re-points | 0.083 | ≈ 20 + 2 S1b forwarders | 1 | 1 | 2 | 1 |

**Recommendation: phase 8 = option S** — the source switcher (`TvSourceSwitchController`, S1a + BADGE)
with an eagerly constructed `TvSourceSwitchApplier` (S1b); the startup/manual gate G moves next as its own
phase (630 lines; or paired with the PikPak engine, ≈ 836, which also gives `pikPakRetryId` its owner in the
same phase — to be measured in the phase-9 inventory). Justification:

- **The bridge is cheaper than the phase-6 estimate assumed.** "G alone would put 51 + 7 cross-unit edits on
  the activity side" counted per reference. Under the Host pattern the 51 S→G references are in-body
  `host.x` substitutions that W needs anyway (as `gate.x`); the activity carries only **11 computed
  forwarders** (re-pointed to `startupGateController.x` in phase 9) plus 7 patches inside G's body that are
  re-substituted when G moves. Total churn S + G ≈ 135 + 7 versus 117 for W (+≈ 20 %).
- **Risk isolation.** Everything that makes W high-risk is in G: the 5-Runnable watchdog protocol, the
  15-statement `onDestroy` block, 24 `playbackListener` + 16 `resolveAndPlay` patches (4 inside templates),
  the 45 reflective watchdog sites, `finish()` dispatch, two Runnable self receivers, 29 of the 31 proofs,
  5 of the 8 Dart edits. Option S touches none of them: 1 lifecycle patch, 1 proof, 1 overload-audit site,
  0 watchdog retargets, 3 Dart edits.
- **Tooling reuse.** S is exactly the phase-6 shape (one controller eagerly constructing one field-less
  sibling, `switcher.`/`applier.` cross-qualifiers, one Host). W with a single Host needs a **new** checker
  class (Host member serving two call shapes of `playItem`: overloads or interface default values) and a
  two-children nested construction.
- **Size.** 768 lines sits at the 800 floor; W is 1,398 (> 1,300 guideline, documented-exception territory).
- Cost of S: two Host objects duplicate ≈ 15 shared names (`stremioSources`, `player`, `payload`, …,
  ≈ +30 activity lines for the rest of the series); the manual-switch transaction temporarily spans
  controller + activity (state single-owned by the activity, reached only through computed forwarders, so
  no behaviour change). BADGE alone or S1a+BADGE alone are strictly worse (phase overhead for 43 lines;
  S1a+BADGE leaves 4 S1b→S1a patches to redo and adds 2 S1a→S1b forwarders).

The full W inventory follows (it is also the G-phase inventory); option S is broken out in its own
section with exact edit lists.

### 9. Hazards

1. **Two-way G↔S coupling** (51 S→G, 7 G→S). W: explicit `gate.`/`sourceSwitch.`/`sourceApplier.`
   qualifiers (65 substitutions). S: 11 Host forwarders to the activity, re-pointed in phase 9.
2. **`ShufflePlaybackAttempt` is a `private` nested class** used in S1b's signature and in the Host's
   `playItem`: one retained visibility patch (`internal`) + destination imports.
3. **`playItem` call shapes through a Host.** G: `playItem(currentIndex, suppressTrakt = true)`; S1b: all four
   arguments named. Per-controller Hosts need no interface defaults (`fun playItem(index, suppressTrakt)` for
   G; 4-parameter forwarder for S, parameter names must match the named arguments). A single W Host needs
   either interface default values copied from 4536–4540 or two overloads — new checker class + negative
   (changed default / swapped overload). `failMoreTorrentSources()` (G, 0-arg) and
   `failManualSourceCandidate(reason)` (1-arg everywhere) forward with the activity's defaults evaluated in
   the forwarder call.
4. **Runnable self `this`** 12394, 12559 (G only) on the reviewed never-substitute list; the reprepare
   `Runnable { … return@Runnable }` (12823–12838) has no `this`.
5. **`finish()`** 12752 (G) → `activity.finish()` dispatches to the activity's `finish()` override (12066,
   progress snapshot). Pin in step 0.
6. **Overload audit sites:** S = 1 (`Toast.makeText(this, …)` 13693); W = 2 (+12744) plus inherited
   `findViewById` ×3 (12578, 12585, 12587; must stay `AppCompatActivity.findViewById(int)`), `isFinishing`,
   `isDestroyed`, `finish`, `runOnUiThread` ×8. No Glide, no view constructors, no context aliases.
7. **Receivers:** `object : Player.Listener` 12943 (S1a), two anonymous `MethodChannel.Result` objects
   13094, 13177 (S1a, no `this`), `object : Runnable` 12377, 12546, `Runnable {` 12428, 12630, 12823, 12936.
   No Host name collides with a `Runnable`/`Player.Listener`/`MethodChannel.Result` member.
8. **Braced templates:** moved code W = 13 (G: `$currentStremioSourceIndex` 12337, 12793, 12883;
   `$hasPlaylistResolver` 12339. S1a: `$currentStremioSourceIndex` 12900, `$hasPlaylistResolver` 13028,

   code under W: 4 (4676, 4682, 14058 ×2) must become braced `${startupGateController.x}`. S1b/BADGE: none.
9. **Earlier-running initializers** (§2) incl. the 11 block-2 fields that move ahead of
   `recoveryStartedAtMs`/`progressReporter`; nothing reads them during construction (progress Host is
   computed).
10. **Controller constructed before its Host target exists**: `iptvChannelStartController` (989) forwards to
    the new controller(s) declared at 1078 (W) / 12920 (S) — computed forwarders only, never invoked during
    property initialization (checker negative exists from phase 3).
11. **`@Volatile activeVodHeaders`** (750) written by S1b through a setter forwarder; the volatile write is
    still to the same field.
12. **Default arguments on moved members** are constants only (`showFailure = true`, `retryId = null`,
    log params, `switchToSourcePlaylist` ×5, `switchToStremioSource` ×2); `$default` bridges move with the
    class; the reflective `schedulePikPakGateReprepare(null)` passes the argument explicitly.
13. **Phase-7 interleaving:** STV's guide-wait members (12985–13025) sit between S1a members; phase 7 also
    patches `onCreate` and `playStremioTvPlaybackMap`, both patched again here. Re-measure on the phase-7

14. **Borrowed handler only:** G and S1a post on `progressHandler` and never clear it; the activity's

15. **Exhaustive checker:** S's applier and BADGE carry no fields — the applier is a pinned eager
    construction inside the switch controller (phase-6 renderer pattern); under W both siblings are pinned

### Behavior and original mutation evidence

**45/45** new tests pass against the original. The fixture uses the actual
activity, inflated layout, source browser, selection/apply methods, retained
gate, retained playItem and MIME discovery. Only the Flutter transport and
player are fakes. Typed reflection pins exact signatures and default bridges;
ShufflePlaybackAttempt retains its original binary name. Movie/unscoped input
fixtures omit absent season/episode keys: explicit JSON-null keys instead
become zero through the already-characterized retained fromMap conversion.

Coverage: manual-before-commit and automatic-recovery selection, committed
manual snapshots, stale resolver supersession and browser same-source guard;
setup/render/current highlight and browser opening; both resolver success,
empty/malformed, error/notImplemented, send-exception and null-bridge paths;
all six success/error/notImplemented replies delivered on bounded worker
threads, with token advancement **after** acceptance and **before** main-loop
drain; live startup cursor read inside the playlist UI block. The latter
acceptance timing is deliberately preserved, without adding a second guard.

Apply coverage includes MediaItem/MIME/header rebuild, volatile active-header
field identity, ordinary and held bookmark seeks, merged audio, IPTV ladder
handoff, PikPak retry identity and the retained reprepare's live guard,
movie/series/collection targeting and resume rules, metadata carry-over and
refresh, singleton catalog identity, exact-episode/manual rejection, specials
fallback toast, all four playItem arguments, startup percent behavior and
shuffle preparation rollback. Badge coverage pins classic show/hide timing,
translations, GONE versus INVISIBLE, synchronous hide and OTT availability.
Outcome coverage pins READY/IDLE messages, IPTV-key suppression, the exact
10-second deadline, current-player cancellation, stale-feedback cleanup and
the existing after-release cancellation in onDestroy.

The MIME fixture is a bounded latch-controlled loopback HEAD server (no public
network or device). It demonstrates headers and discovered MIME recursion,
and rejects a result superseded while IO is blocked. All worker/server threads
are joined; owned coroutine jobs and handlers are cancelled during cleanup.

**49/49 original mutations killed**, covering every new test. Six proofs add a
second UI token guard (each callback branch); six remove the existing pre-post
stale guard (each callback branch). Every proof ran on detached original
53906805d + the final six test files, whose fixture signature matches the
passing control run. Each archived run contains exactly its one named case and
an AssertionError/ComparisonFailure. No compile failures, empty runs or
worker/server crashes were accepted. Exact replacements/scopes, patches,
Gradle logs, XML and failure stacks are under `p8/mutations/`; definitions in
`p8/mutations.json`, runner `p8/run_mutations.py`, control XML and identities in
`p8/original-control*`. The detached original worktree is removed after use.

other gate-2 units that already call into the gate (fetch-more S2: 10 gate refs; episode fetch EF; status
pill), as the phase-6 re-plan listed them. Justification:

- **A is already at the top of the risk scale**: 93 activity patches (24 in `playbackListener`, 16 in
  `resolveAndPlay` incl. 2 unbraced templates, 15 in `onDestroy`, 7 in `parsePayload`), 15 forwarder
  re-points in two earlier-phase properties, 29 inert proofs, the 5-Runnable watchdog protocol, `finish()`
  virtual dispatch, 70 reflective test sites. B adds no relief to any of these.
- **Pairing does not actually settle `pikPakRetryId`.** Its writers stay spread over three owners whatever
  we do: `playPikPakVideoWithRetry` (playback start, retained until that phase), the phase-8 applier
  (`pikPakRetryId++` through a Host `var`) and `cancelPikPakRetry`. The only gate use is 3 **reads** inside
  `schedulePikPakGateReprepare`, two of them at fire time inside the reprepare `Runnable`; under A they go
  through a computed Host `val` forwarder to the activity field — live, single owner, no snapshot — and the
  phase-8 test `Apply.retainedPikPakReprepareReadsLiveRetryIdAtFireTime` already pins it.
- **B adds new hazard classes to the riskiest phase**: two `::x.isInitialized` readiness getters
  (`startupGateStatus` 6677, `pikPakReactivationIndicator` 6691), an owned `Handler` (`pikPakRetryHandler`)
  whose clear moves behind a controller in `onDestroy`, 4 more Runnable self receivers, 3 more lifecycle
  patches (`onPause`, `onDestroy` ×2), a timing-heavy step 0 (backoff 0/2/4/8/16/18 s + 10 s metadata
  window, ≈ 70 s virtual time per exhaustion path), and 15 more reflective sites.
- **Deferral is cheap**: under A the PK bodies take 8 patches into the gate (`startupGateController.x`);
  the later PK phase turns those into 8 host substitutions + 5 PK-Host forwarders and re-points 1 gate Host
  forwarder (`pikPakRetryId`) and the 6 phase-8 switcher PK forwarders (needed under A+B too). Extra churn
  ≈ 9 edits. A+B would save those but add ≈ +20 % edits to this phase (+4 net patches, +6 re-points,
  +3 proofs, +2 readiness getters, +3 lifecycle patches, +42 substitutions).
- If a reviewer still prefers pairing, use **sibling controllers (B2)** — gate at slot 1078, PK at its own
  slot 1384, cross edges only through computed Host forwarders — not the nested form (B1), which would move
  the `Handler(Looper.getMainLooper())` allocation ≈ 300 initializers earlier and grow one Host to ≈ 42.

### 9. Hazards

1. **`finish()` virtual dispatch** (12755, exhaustion branch of `failStartupCandidate`, inside the
   `startupFailoverDispatching` `try`): must become `activity.finish()` (`activity: AppCompatActivity`),
   compiled as `invokevirtual` so it still runs the activity override (12069: one-shot final
   `progressReporter.sendProgress(completed = false)` guarded by `finishProgressAttempted`,
   `PlaybackReturnHandoff.markReturning(sourcePersistenceSessionId)`, `recordPlaybackLifecycle("finish_requested")`,
   then `super.finish()`). Never a Host forwarder with logic, never a `super`/non-virtual form. Order to pin:
   `startupSourcesExhausted = true` → `startupFailoverCursor = null` → `hideStatusPill()` → Toast → `finish()`
   → (override reads exhausted/cursor **through the progress Host, i.e. the same gate fields**, so the final
   progress stays muted) → `finally { startupFailoverDispatching = false }`. Step 0 asserts the override's
   observable effects on the gate-exhaustion path (handoff marker, lifecycle record, `finishProgressAttempted`,
   no progress invocation) and the compiled audit records the `finish()V` call as `invokevirtual`.
2. **Unbraced templates.** Moved code (4): 12340 `$currentStremioSourceIndex`, 12342 `$hasPlaylistResolver`,
   12796 `$currentStremioSourceIndex`, 12886 `$currentStremioSourceIndex` → `${host.x}`. Retained code (4):
   4679, 4685 `$startupFailoverGeneration`; 14019 `$startupTryNextOnFailure`, `$startupMaxAttempts` →
   `${startupGateController.x}`. Braced already (plain qualification): bindViews 2502 (×3); G `${…}` forms
   12340 `${stremioSources.size}`, 12603 `${if (isStremioTvMode) …}`, 12628/12671/12741/12768
   `${startupSourceFields(currentStremioSourceIndex)}`. Gate-owned names in templates (12341
   `$startupTryNextOnFailure`, `$STARTUP_FAILOVER_TIMEOUT_MS` 12407) stay as written. PK: none.
3. **Runnable self `this`** — never substitute: G 12397, 12562 (`object : Runnable`); PK 6617, 6637, 6649,
   6662 (`object : Runnable` in `waitForPikPakMetadata`). `Runnable {` SAM lambdas 12431, 12633, 12826 have

  substitutions against phase-8-patched text); negatives: unbraced host template (moved and retained),
  `finish()` routed through a Host forwarder or a non-virtual form, snapshot `val pikPakRetryId`/`player`
  in the gate Host, same-name capture (Host declaring `cancelSourceSwitchWait` or `failStartupCandidate`),
  an `onDestroy` statement reordered or folded into a controller call, a missed re-point (forwarder still
  targeting the activity member, which no longer exists → compile) and an extra edit in a patched property,
  an omitted block-2 proof; compiled overload audit (Toast, 3× `findViewById`, `finish` invokevirtual); all
  earlier destinations (incl. the two phase-8 files) frozen against the phase-8 merge.
- **Step 0 gaps beyond the existing 14 watchdog, 1 progress and 45 phase-8 cases**: commit grace/slate for
  both manual and startup commits (AIOStreams 1 s duration grace via the 200 ms checks); manual reject
  restore (snapshot restore order, `manualSourceRestoreInProgress`, `player.stop` → `rebuildPlaylistContent`
  → `playItem(…, suppressTrakt = true)`, pill vs hide, `superseded` path); `armStartupCandidate` gate UI
  (debrid-first-open GONE, heading animation values, focus to `startup_back`, explanation/status texts,
  Stremio TV without deadline); `failStartupCandidate` (`startupSourceFailed` payload incl.
  `sourcePersistenceSessionId`, failed-release keys and candidate predicate, PikPak acquisition guard,
  recovery-fetch branch + 30 s fallback, exhaustion toast texts + **`finish()` through the override**);
  `failStartupResolution` ignore path; watchdog extension caps (PikPak 120 s, buffering 45 s, 3 s recheck);
  reprepare guard matrix; `startupSourceFields` sanitisation; the two `DiagnosticFileLog` records;
  `resolveAndPlay` stale-generation/stale-manual discards and initial-resolve failure; `parsePayload`
  writes (clamp 1..10, empty provider → null); `sendFinished` map; `onDestroy` (pending gate callbacks
  never fire, late resolve discarded after the generation bump, final snapshot before the clear).
  B would add: backoff schedule, token cancellation, success path, exhaustion hand-off order
  (shuffle → manual → startup → toast + 1.5 s `playNext` on the owned handler), overlay mirror to the gate
  status, uninitialized-indicator guard, `onPause`/`onDestroy` cancellation.

### 12. Follow-ups found while mapping (not fixed)

- The gate's 30 s recovery fallback (12731) and `missing-source` post (12784) are retired only by the
  wholesale `progressHandler` clear (unchanged).
- `waitForPikPakMetadata`'s local `checkHandler` is never cleared; it stops on its next 500 ms tick via the
  `pikPakRetryId` check (existing follow-up).
- `onDestroy` does not reset `startupSourcesExhausted`/`startupRecoveryConsumed` — intended, `sendFinished`
  (14435) reads them; pin as-is.
- PK's exhaustion toast path checks `isFinishing` but not `isDestroyed` (6573); pin as-is.
- Dart rows 2, 3, 5, 11 are whole-file `contains`; consider `_between` ranges of the owning gate functions
  in a separate test-only change.

Original: `c4906cd2f`; Step T: `6b7bd2821`. Production remains byte-identical

resolution, parse clamps/defaults and teardown are also covered.

## Phase 9 step 0b

On original `c4906cd2f`, added 11 boundary characterizations; all 28
method-scoped mutations fail their named test on an assertion. Exact Claude
survivors k04/k09/k10/k12 are included: existing child focus stays on the
gate, debrid first-open leaves outside focus alone, hidden controls keep the
badge hidden, and startup/manual commits replace the actual progress pulse
and report at five seconds. The late failed-row Flutter reply is delivered
while recovery keeps the activity live: it cannot replace the payload or
touch the player. A separate manual-failure reply pins that token bump.

The sweep covers every moved focus/controls visibility gate, the restart
calls in both commits, removals of every timeout/commit-check/reprepare in
commit and fail, both switcher listener/timeout cancellations, the failure
stop and generation bump, startup rearming, orphaned manual timeout
replacement, and cancellation through the retained PikPak retry caller.
Commit paths retain the resolver token; failure paths invalidate it.
Callbacks are checked in the real borrowed queue, not only nulled fields.
Animation frames are drained deterministically while observing ticker
boundaries. No production code or behavior changed.

Evidence: `p9/step0b/` contains definitions, dependency hashes, full Gradle
logs and XML. `claude-survivors-rerun/` reruns the four exact patches against
all 51 phase-9 cases plus the 14 watchdog cases (65 identities), with named
assertion kills. JVM `p9-step0b`: 810 identities = 809 pass + the same
pre-existing focus failure; `p9-step0` retains all 799 identities/statuses
with 11 passing additions only, stable tested tree and complete XML. The
post-0b owner rescan still requires 30 routes; no new public function needed.

### Summary and recommendation

| option | lines out | activity patches | re-points | new Hosts | proofs | lifecycle patches | reflective work | Dart | new files |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **R** (recommended): 3 sibling controllers — `TvStatusPillController` (PILL), `TvPikPakRetryController` (PK), `TvSourceFetchController` (S2+EF) | 640 (+4 companion) | **27 in 13 decls** | **17 forwarders / 20 token edits in 3 properties** (subtitle 3, switcher 9/12, gate 5) | 2 + 11 + 22 = 35 members | **4** (no classifier extension) | 3 (`onPause` 13544; `onDestroy` 13638, 13639) | 7 owner-map entries + 1 watchdog `when` branch + 1 `ShufflePlaybackFlowTest` helper line; 28 direct (main) + 7 direct (p9 branch) + 23 `pill()` indirect sites | **1 edit + 1 file read** | 3 files: ≈ 75 + ≈ 240 + ≈ 425 |
| R + `playPikPakVideoWithRetry` rides with PK | 694 | 22 in 13 decls (−6, +1 in `startPlayback`) | 17 | PK Host 11 → ≈ 21 | 4 | 3 | same | same | PK ≈ 300 |
| R′: S2 and EF as separate siblings | 640 | **34 in 14** (S2 must own in-flight state to have a slot: +7 incl. `parsePayload`) | 18 (+ gate `moreSourcesLoadingMode`) | + EF→S2 `adoptSourceList` forwarder | 6 | 3 | + 2 map entries (none reflected today) | 1 + 1 | 4 files |
| R″: one combined controller | 640 | 27 | 17 (all to one target) | 1 × ≈ 45 | **6** (slot 1354 → PK fields, EF field run earlier) | 3 | same | same | 1 file ≈ 770 (near cap, poor cohesion) |

**Recommendation: phase 10 = option R** (≈ 644 moved lines, ≈ 740 new-file lines). The 640 lines are
below the ~700 target, but:
- the cluster is closed;
- the only natural rider, `playPikPakVideoWithRetry` (54), is a media-start path. The plan assigns it to the
  playback-start phase, and it would add ≈ 10 forwarders to save 5 patches;
- the next unit (IPTV core + EPG + VOD, ≈ 2,500) cannot be paired without blowing past 1,200 lines.

Reasons:

- **It finishes the gate's recovery protocol.** After phase 9 the gate reaches all four sub-units through
  5 Host forwarders (`requestMoreTorrentSources`, `failMoreTorrentSources`, `pikPakRetryId`, `hideStatusPill`,
  `showStatusPillTransient`). The PK and S2 bodies carry 18 `startupGateController.` tokens left by phase 9.
- **Low lifecycle risk.**
  - Only 3 lifecycle statements change, each a one-token in-place patch (`onPause` 13544, `onDestroy`
    13638/13639).
  - There is no `finish()`, no override dispatch, and no `onStart`/`onStop`/`finish` reference.
  - It needs no initializer-classifier extension: `Runnable { … }`, constants and
    `Handler(Looper.getMainLooper())` are all supported already.
- **One owner per piece of state.**

  | state | owner after phase 10 |
  |---|---|
  | `pikPakRetryId`/`Count`/`isPikPakRetrying`/`pikPakRetryHandler` | PK |
  | `episodeFetchInFlight` | fetch controller |
  | `statusPill` | pill controller |
  | `stremioResolutionToken` | stays in the activity (shared with retained `resolveAndPlay`/`discoverProtectedMime`, gate, switcher) |
  | S2's payload-derived flags/lists | stay in the activity (written by `parsePayload`) |

- **Why S2 and EF are one controller.**
  - The checker only allows a controller slot at a **removed original field**
    (`kotlin_move_partition.py:43–52`, "added slot must be a removed original field").
  - S2 owns no field unless it takes the in-flight state, which costs +7 patches incl. `parsePayload` and
    +2 proofs. EF owns exactly one field (`episodeFetchInFlight`).
  - Merging them gives the pair a clean slot. It also turns the only EF→S2 edge (`adoptSourceList` ×2) into
    an internal call. Both units ask Flutter for a replacement source list and adopt it append-only.
- **Status pill ends with only 2 activity callers.**
  - Production call sites total **40**: 19 direct in the activity (at the phase-8 merge), 17 in the switcher
    files and 4 in the subtitle controller, plus 6 Host forwarders.
  - After phase 9: 14 direct (the gate's 5 move into the gate file), 8 forwarders.
  - After phase 10: **2 direct** (`playbackListener` 1829, `playShowShuffle` 5489) and 9 forwarders.
  - EF's 11 and S2's 1 move with their units.

Risk: **medium.**
- PK is timing-heavy: backoff 0/2/4/8/16/18 s on a 10 s metadata window, ≈ 70 s virtual time per
  exhaustion path.
- EF and S2 have **no** existing JVM characterization, apart from the gate-recovery handoff the phase-9
  tests drive through `requestMoreTorrentSources`.
- 17 re-points touch three earlier-phase properties (phases 4, 8/9 and 9).

Behaviour to pin in step 0: inside `onDestroy`, `cancelPikPakRetry()` → `hidePikPakRetryOverlay()` runs its
`runOnUiThread` body inline. On API ≥ 17 `isDestroyed` is already `true` during `onDestroy`
(`performDestroy` sets `mDestroyed` first), so the hide returns early. The explicit 13641–13645 cleanup is
what hides the indicator. Characterize under Robolectric SDK 28, do not assume.

### 9. Hazards

1. **Runnable / object self-references**: never substitute. PK `waitForPikPakMetadata`'s `object : Runnable`
   `this` at 6617, 6637, 6649, 6662. Everything else needs no runnable-receiver row:
   - PILL `Runnable { hideStatusPill() }` and the PK 1.5 s lambda have no `this`;
   - EF/S2 `object : MethodChannel.Result` bodies contain no `this`.
2. **Activity `this` / overload / inherited-receiver audit sites**:

   | unit | sites |
   |---|---|
   | PILL | `TextView(this)` constructor 11822; implicit `findViewById<ViewGroup>(android.R.id.content)` 11840 |
   | PK | `Toast.makeText(this, …)` 6575; `runOnUiThread` ×3, `isFinishing` ×4, `isDestroyed` ×2 |
   | fetch | `Toast.makeText(this, …)` 13181; `runOnUiThread` ×15 (inside anonymous `Result` objects — implicit outer receiver), `isFinishing` ×2, `isDestroyed` ×2 (one pair inside the `post` lambda) |

   No Glide, view constructors beyond `TextView`, context aliases or `finish()`.
3. **`isFinishing`/`isDestroyed` asymmetries to pin as-is:**
   - PK exhaustion toast checks only `!isFinishing` (6573);
   - EF `Result` callbacks never check finishing/destroyed: their only liveness is the token,
     `shouldContinue` and `yieldEpisodeFetchToQueuedShuffle()` (which includes `!isFinishing && !isDestroyed`);
     `notImplemented` paths skip even the token check;
   - S2 addon-fetch callbacks have no guard; `applyMoreTorrentSources` guards at entry.
4. **Templates**: there are **no unbraced** host-name templates in the cluster.
   - One braced host reference, `${stremioSources.size}` 13054, gets plain qualification inside the braces.
   - `${PIKPAK_MAX_RETRIES + 1}` ×2 resolves to the file-private const unchanged.
   - EF/S2 `$label`, `$directionLabel`, `$mode`, `$before`, `$errorCode`, `$errorMessage`, `${curItem?…}`
     are locals.
   - A checker negative still proves an unbraced host template fails.
5. **`apply`/`also` receivers in PILL**: `host.dp(…)` sits inside `TextView.apply {}` and
   `GradientDrawable.apply {}`. I confirmed that neither `TextView`/`View` nor `GradientDrawable` has a
   `host` or `activity` member. EF's `hashMapOf(…).apply { put(…) }` references no host name.
6. **Named arguments / defaults through Hosts**:
   - `guideAdjacent(…, allowResolverFallback = true)`: the forwarder parameter must be named
     `allowResolverFallback`, with no interface default.
   - The gate forwarder `failMoreTorrentSources()` is 0-arg: the callee default `alreadyCleared = false` is
     evaluated in the forwarder call.
   - Inbound EF calls with named args (`autoAdvance =`, `suppressResume =`, `shuffleAttempt =`,
     `shouldContinue =`, `onUnavailable =`) go **directly** to the controller, not through a Host.
   - `waitForPikPakMetadata`'s `additionalMonitoringMs = 0`, `requestAdjacentEpisodeFetch`'s
     `autoAdvance = false`/`direction = 1`, and `requestEpisodeFetch`'s `suppressResume = autoAdvance`
     (an earlier parameter) all move with the class.
7. **Prefix increment through a Host var**: `val token = ++host.stremioResolutionToken` ×2. Fixture plus test:
   the captured token equals the post-increment value, and the field is written once.
8. **Controllers constructed before their forward targets** (all computed reads, never at construction):

   | forwarder in | constructed at | forwards to |
   |---|---|---|
   | gate Host | 1078 | PILL 1354, PK 1384, fetch 12124 |
   | subtitle Host | 1213 | PILL 1354 |
   | fetch Host | 12124 | switcher ≈ 12899, gate 1078, PILL |

   The existing "reads Host during construction" negative covers this.
9. **Live reads inside deferred work**:
   - PK: `pikPakRetryId` (Runnable plus callback), `player` and `isStremioTvMode` (Runnable), and
     `startupGateController.startupFailoverCursor` (lambda) — all via the owner field or computed Host;
   - EF: `stremioResolutionToken` and `payload`/`currentIndex` (error path) at reply time;
   - `playShowShuffle`'s 50 ms re-check of `episodeFetchInFlight` through the patched controller read;
   - the gate's 30 s fallback reading `moreSourcesLoadingMode` via its (unchanged) Host.

   A snapshot `val` anywhere is a negative.
10. **Owned vs borrowed handlers**:
    - `pikPakRetryHandler` becomes PK-owned. The activity's `onDestroy` clear stays in place as
      `pikPakRetryController.pikPakRetryHandler.removeCallbacksAndMessages(null)`; `cancelPikPakRetry`
      clears it too (unchanged).
    - `externalSubtitleHandler` and `progressHandler` are borrowed; the controllers never clear them
      wholesale.
11. **Same-name capture**:
    - the PILL Host must not declare pill names;
    - the PK Host must not declare PK names, gate names (`cancelPikPakGateReprepare`,
      `schedulePikPakGateReprepare`, `failManualSourceCandidate`, `failStartupCandidate`,
      `startupFailoverCursor`) or switcher names;

      name.

    A missed `host.` on `startupGateController.`/`sourceSwitchController.` cannot compile in the new files,
    but it is a checker negative too.
12. **Patched earlier-phase properties**:
    - `subtitleController` (phase-4 `added`; first patch since phase 4, phase-5 sleep precedent);
